name: Hammock Camping
tagline: For campers sleeping off the ground between trees in three-season forest conditions.
description: A starting point for 1-4 nights of hammock camping in forested terrain from spring through fall, on foot or near the car. Assumes suitable live trees are available, nights can be cool enough to need bottom insulation, and bugs may be out. Adapt insulation to the forecast lows, carry a ground backup where trees are uncertain, and confirm hammocks are allowed where you are going.
considerations: Check that hammocks are allowed; some state and local parks prohibit hanging anything from trees.
Plan on live, healthy trees at least 6 inches in diameter with no dead branches overhead; never hang from dead trees.
Expect to need bottom insulation (underquilt or pad) once nights drop below roughly 70 F.
Camp at least 200 feet from water on an existing site; hammocks still need a durable spot underneath.
Check current fire restrictions and bear food-storage rules just as you would for tent camping.
Check the forecast for wind and rain; tarp size and pitch matter more in a hammock than in a tent.

sources.title: 2025 Leave No Trace Hammock Camping Guidelines
Beat the Chill! Practical Ways to Stay Warm While Hammock Camping

items.text: Confirmed with the land manager that hammocks are permitted
Map and compass, with likely hang sites noted
Forecast checked for lows, wind, and rain
Backcountry or campground permit where required
Ground backup (pad and bivy or tent) where trees are uncertain
Tree straps of 1-inch or wider webbing (no rope or cord on bark)
items.note: Wrap once, hang loose, hang under 5 ft high, and never nail or screw anything into trees.

items.text: Suspension hardware: whoopie slings, buckles, or carabiners

items.note: Essential in mosquito and tick season.

items.text: Rain tarp long enough to cover the hammock with overhang
Underquilt rated for the expected low
items.note: A pad can substitute but shifts when you lie diagonally.

items.text: Top quilt or sleeping bag rated for the expected low
Drip lines on the suspension so rain does not run into the hammock
Tarp with doors or a larger winter tarp for wind
Sleeping pad as backup insulation and for ground camping
Snakeskins or stuff sacks for a fast pack-up
Bear canister or hang kit per local rules
items.note: Check current food-storage rules; never keep food in the hammock.

items.text: Non-cotton base layers and hiking clothes
Warm hat and gloves (hammocks run cold)
Dry socks and a sleep layer
Trowel for catholes 6-8 in deep, 200 ft from water
Toilet paper in a zip bag
Extra cord and a spare guyline
Repair tape, needle and thread, spare buckle
Trekking poles (double as tarp porch poles)
